clue.text: Young flower is one containing empty seeds

indicators.note: containing puts the shortened seeds inside the flower word

parts.note: one here stands for a flower, picking up the definition: a bloom

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its shell, so seeds loses its inside letters

parts.note: empty seeds keeps only the first and last letters of seeds

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a young plant that holds seed cases with nothing inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'flower', giving BLOOM; 'empty seeds' leaves just S and S, which 'containing' places inside BLOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the flowering of a plant, the early stage before fruit sets, so a young flower.

clue.text: Special capsule made by 7

indicators.note: special suggests something specially made, so the letters of capsule are rearranged

explanation.surface: A special capsule produced by the solution to 7 down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 refers to 7 down, a shoemaker, who makes lace-up shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace-ups are shoes fastened with laces, exactly what a cobbler or shoemaker produces.

clue.text: Small bird's back

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: The back of a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship, so the back end.

clue.text: Verona production featuring Romeo went on for too long

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the Romeo letter goes inside
a production of a play reworks it, so the letters of Verona are rearranged

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Verona staging of Romeo and Juliet ran over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' looks like Shakespeare's hero, set in Verona, but gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that overran exceeded its allotted time, carrying on longer than it should.

clue.text: An essential, like round fruit …

indicators.note: turning something round sends it the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an essential is a must, something you cannot do without
as means like, in the sense of in the manner of

explanation.surface: A shopper lists a staple item, comparing it to a round piece of fruit, the sentence trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a description of the fruit but is the signal to turn the letters about. The trailing dots only link the surface to 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small loose-skinned citrus, a kind of mandarin orange, so an example of fruit.

clue.text: Heartless pussycat misbehaves and makes trouble

indicators.note: a word that misbehaves goes out of order, so its letters are rearranged
heartless removes the middle letters of pussycat

explanation.surface: A cruel cat behaves badly and causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaves' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal for PUSCAT, pussycat without its central SY.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly or cause trouble, as children or machines do.

clue.text: One has a last desperate smoke — hear?

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters of smoke and hear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A condemned person asks to be heard over a final cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler shapes shoes on, not a final thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A last is a cobbler's wooden foot model, so the craftsman who has one is a shoemaker.

clue.text: Postman Pat has this wild animal biting villagers, primarily!

indicators.note: biting means taking in the teeth, so the rearranged letters hold the next letter
wild suggests disorder, so the letters of animal are rearranged
primarily picks the first letter of villagers

explanation.surface: Postman Pat keeps a wild creature that bites the villagers.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV character who delivers post around a village in his red van.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman Pat drives a red Royal Mail delivery vehicle, the vehicle used to carry post.

clue.text: Crazy golfers largely tell you — relax!

indicators.note: crazy suggests things gone mad, so the letters are rearranged
largely means most of the word, so tell loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Mad golfers mostly tell you to take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Crazy golf is a British name for minigolf, which strengthens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To let yourself go is to drop your inhibitions and unwind, so an instruction to relax.

clue.text: … top with whipped cream right away!

indicators.note: cream that is whipped is beaten up, so its letters are churned into a new order
right away says the letter for right is taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: Someone urges a dessert be finished with whipped cream immediately, continuing from the fruit of the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once' but asks you to remove R; the remaining letters of CREAM, 'whipped', make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of something, so it is a synonym of top.

clue.text: Choose fancy iron, finally metric, using computer control

parts.note: to elect is to choose, as voters do

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, so the letters of iron are reimagined in a new order
finally points to the last letter of metric

explanation.surface: Advice on picking a decorative iron that works in metric units and is driven by a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy iron' looks like an ornate appliance; 'fancy' is the signal to rearrange IRON into RONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something electronic runs on circuits and microchips, the kind of device operated by computer control.

clue.text: Boss terribly hungover? Not he!

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of hungover are jumbled
Not he says the letters of he are left out of the jumble

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the boss is badly hungover and is told it is not him.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H and E out of HUNGOVER and rearrange the rest. Guvnor is British slang, short for governor, for a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Guvnor is informal British usage for the person in charge, an employer or manager.

clue.text: I've just been over my preparation — getting to grips with university

indicators.note: getting to grips with means holding, so the mixed letters hold the university letters
a preparation is a mixture made up, so the letters of over my are mixed

parts.note: OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A student says they have revised their preparation while coping with university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've just been' is what a game player says before handing over: it is now the other player's turn. The OU is Britain's Open University.
explanation.definitionFit: In a board game, having just taken a turn means it is now the opponent's go, the phrase said to them.

clue.text: Roast tuna salad for Major Tom?

indicators.note: a salad is a mixture of ingredients, so the letters of roast tuna are tossed together

explanation.surface: A menu suggestion of roast tuna salad for someone called Major Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: Major Tom is the spaceman of David Bowie's song Space Oddity, so the name is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Major Tom is a fictional space traveller in Bowie's songs, an example of a spaceman.

clue.text: Cyclists may sound familiar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a cyclist may do to warn others, sound the bell on the handlebars
second meaning: to seem familiar, to jog the memory

explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' does double duty in the surface: cyclists sound a bell, and something that rings a bell sounds familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a cyclist's warning action and an idiom for something stirring a vague memory.

clue.text: Found in street: family that's poor …

indicators.note: found in says the family word sits inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: kin means family, one's relatives

explanation.surface: A poor family is discovered living on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money. The ellipsis carries the same construction on to 17 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is informal British slang for penniless, having no money at all.

clue.text: … and writer that's exhausted

indicators.note: and says the writer joins the family of the previous clue, likewise found in street, so it goes inside

parts.note: the ellipsis carries over 'Found in street' from the previous clue: ST, the abbreviation for street, with the writer found inside it
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: Continuing the street scene: a writer living there is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue cannot be solved alone: the leading dots stand for 'Found in street' from 16 across, and 'and' says the same treatment applies here.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up or worn out, with no energy left, so tired out.

clue.text: Ripe for development around dry open grassland

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters on both sides of the drying word
something ready for development is to be reworked, so the letters of ripe are rearranged

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it

explanation.surface: Arid open grassland is ripe for building on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' looks like an adjective for the grassland but is the verb AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large area of flat, treeless grassland, as in North America.

clue.text: Online club's bad progress, endlessly initiated and interrupted by you, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says it is the sound of you that counts, the letter U

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U; the clue uses it twice, initiating and interrupting

indicators.note: interrupted by says the second U breaks into the scrambled letters
bad progress is going wrong, so the letters of the shortened word are scrambled
endlessly removes the final letter of progress

explanation.surface: An internet group complains about its poor progress, started and disrupted by people like you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiated' puts one U at the start; 'interrupted by' puts the other inside PROGRES (progress less its last S) once that is rearranged by 'bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A user group is a forum of people who use a product, often meeting online, so a club.

clue.text: Gloat when piece is in ruin

indicators.note: is in places the piece word inside ruin

parts.note: a bit is a piece of something

explanation.surface: Someone gloats when a piece of something lies in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub it in is to keep reminding someone of their failure, a way to crow over them.

clue.text: Centurions set out having been ordered to find partner for lion

indicators.note: set out here means the letters of set are removed from the fodder
having been ordered means put into a new order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Roman centurions march out under orders to find a mate for a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' reads as 'departed' but means remove S, E and T from CENTURIONS before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion and the unicorn are the paired supporters on the British royal coat of arms.

clue.text: Support medical treatment that hurts

parts.note: a pill is a tablet taken as medicine
ow is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their supportive medical treatment is painful.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a cushion that supports the head in bed.

clue.text: Luxurious pad mostly, one in a tall building

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of pad
building means constructing, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A luxurious flat, mostly, one of those in a tower block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the tower in the picture but signals that I, A and TALL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatial means like a palace, grand and lavish, so luxurious.

clue.text: Part of job of fine scientist

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scientist does part of a fine job.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert, especially one doing research.

clue.text: Left wearing reasonable gift

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the fair word wraps around the left letter

parts.note: fair means reasonable or just

explanation.surface: A sensible present was left on.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural talent or aptitude, as is a gift for something.

clue.text: Go ahead and agree on flight taking off at first

indicators.note: taking off at first removes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Permission is given and a flight is cleared to take off first.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop A, O and F, the first letters of 'agree', 'on' and 'flight', and the rest spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A green light is permission to proceed, like the traffic signal, so a go-ahead.

clue.text: Ring involved in law-breaking is missing

indicators.note: involved in places the ring letter inside the other letters
law-breaking: the word law is broken up, its letters rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A criminal gang that broke the law has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: AWOL is a military abbreviation for Absent Without Leave.
explanation.definitionFit: AWOL describes a soldier absent without leave, and more widely anyone who has gone missing.

clue.text: Gushes about the Spanish guys!

indicators.note: about puts the gushing word around the Spanish article

parts.note: gushes means flows, as water does
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses about the Spanish men.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellows are men or chaps in informal speech, so a synonym of guys.

clue.text: First fashionable face

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
the face of a building is its front

explanation.surface: A trendy face comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in front is to lead, ahead of everyone else, so first in position.
